author: Old North News
title: Moody's affirms Cary's Aaa bond rating, citing strong financial management
text:
Moody’s affirms Cary’s Aaa bond rating, citing strong financial management
Moody’s has affirmed the Town of Cary’s Aaa bond rating, the highest possible credit rating for municipal governments, according to a July 8 announcement from the town. The affirmation reflects Cary's long-standing financial discipline, strong reserves, and effective long-term planning.
The Moody’s decision places Cary among a select group of communities nationwide that maintain this top-tier credit status. This rating is expected to help lower borrowing costs for capital projects such as parks, greenways, streets, public safety facilities, and utility infrastructure used by residents.
Interim Town Manager Russ Overton said, “Moody’s reaffirming our Aaa status says a lot about the discipline of this organization and staff, as well as Cary’s strong financial position. For decades, our team has taken a steady, careful approach to budgeting and planning. Because of that, Cary’s residents benefit from lower borrowing costs and our ability to keep investing in the projects our community depends on.”
The Aaa rating is attributed to consistent sound budgeting practices and responsible planning that position the town to manage growth while maintaining fiscal stability. More information about Cary's financial stewardship can be found at carync.gov/acfr. Details on how bonds are sold for important local projects are available at carync.gov/municipalbonds.
